section.title: Logic
section.item: Logical not, written as ! too.
Logical and, written as && too. It binds LOOSER than the comparisons across the whole expression, so a < b and c < d reads the way it looks.

Bitwise exclusive or. Written as ^ too - and that catches people out: x ^ 2 is NOT x squared, it is x xor 2. It returns a number, just never the one you meant. Write x ** 2 for the square.

Bitwise or. Careful with precedence: it binds as tightly as multiplication, not as loosely as addition, so 1 + 6 | 3 is 1 + (6 | 3), which is 8. Brackets say it plainly.
Bitwise exclusive or, written as a call. The sign for it is xor.
